questions.question: OP-01/O64 (freeze): RFC-0029 R2 lets a record freeze only when each open item names what it blocks, and O3 to O12 and O42 name nothing. Scenario: the spec flow for OP-01 reaches D11's clause (handle state, O3, shared: State) and needs to know if it can write it now. What does each item block?

options.label: Per item, as listed (Recommended)
options.description: Each shared item holds back only OP-01's spec clauses for its own decisions, until OP-01's flow decides where they land (shared.md says that flow does the landing). O5 also waits on OP-21. O6 and O42 block nothing here. Every item then names what it blocks, so R2's freeze can apply. Source: O64, shared.md intro and Lands elsewhere, RFC-0029 R2 as O64 quotes it.
options.preview:
O3  shared State: blocks OP-01's spec clause for D11 until OP-01's flow decides where it lands.
O4  shared timeout bound: blocks the clauses for D12-D14, D57, D58, D97 until landed.
O5  shared Lifetime: blocks the clause for D18's 'handle's lifetime ends' column; blocked by OP-21's flow.
O6  for OP-03-05, OP-12-15: blocks nothing here; a session that cannot keep D21's premise reopens D21.
O7  shared unhomed: blocks the clauses for D23, D63, D64, D82, D83, D87 until a home is named.
O8  shared Handle: blocks the clause for D24 (with D81) until landed.
O9  shared error layer: blocks every failure-category clause (O9's list) until OP-01's flow names the layer's home.
O10 shared Lifetime: blocks the clause for D37 until landed.
O11 shared retry: blocks the clause for D38's never-retried list until landed.
O12 shared unhomed: blocks the clause for D43's static/conditioned rule (D82) until a home is named.
O42 for O6's sessions: blocks nothing here.

options.label: All: blocks nothing here
options.description: OP-01's spec writes every clause now. The landing flow moves or cites them later. Less is held back, but a clause could be written twice (in OP-01's spec and in a shared.md section), and the two copies can drift.

options.label: Shared items block the freeze
options.description: The record stays unfrozen until every shared item has landed. Safest for drift, but OP-01 would wait on OP-21's flow (O5) and on homes for O7 and O12. That contradicts R2, which lets shared: items stand open in a frozen record.

questions.question: OP-01/O64 (freeze): RFC-0029 R2 lets a record freeze only when each open item names what it blocks, and O3 to O12 and O42 name nothing. Scenario: the spec flow for OP-01 reaches D11's clause (handle state, O3, shared: State) and needs to know if it can write it now. What does each item block?

End check, D104's O9 list: D104 says O9's list is every AX-10 decision plus every decision whose Amends names one of D27 to D34. Its list, "D84 to D86", includes D85. D85 is AX-15 and amends only D61, so it fits neither rule. What happens to D85?

options.label: Drop D85 (Recommended)
options.description: The list then matches its stated derivation. Nothing is lost: D85 only brings D61's reason in line with D62, and D62's meaning of changed is already on the list.

options.label: Keep D85, widen rule
options.description: The derivation also counts decisions that amend a listed decision (D85 amends D61). Of the record's Amends lines, that adds D85 alone. The rule is then longer, and the next transitive amendment must be added too.

questions.question: End check, D104's O7 list against D105: O7's list is "D23, D63, D64, D82, D83 and D87". D105's Read-after-write Decided-by column also names D76 and D105, which state the same normal value in D43's table. D108's O7 copies D104's list. How is the list kept?

options.label: As is, name derivation (Recommended)
options.description: D104's check adds: O7 names the decisions that decide the behaviour; D76 and D105 only restate it in D43's table. Nothing changes in D108. The list then states its derivation, as principle 9 asks.

options.label: Add D76 and D105
options.description: O7's list in D104 and D108 gains D76 and D105, matching D105's column. The two lists agree, but O7 then names restatements beside the decisions.

questions.question: End check, D108's O11 against its reason: D108 says no clause is written before its home is known. Yet it has O11 block only "D38's list of failures never retried". O11's summary also covers what the library retries and the per-store bound (default 3 attempts per request). Under D108 those clauses could be written first. What does O11 block?

options.label: D38's library-retry clauses (Recommended)
options.description: Blocked: what is retried, the per-request bound and its default, and the never-retried list (D74). D38's caller-level table, with D60 and D98, is not blocked: it is OP-01's own AX-13 row. The outcome then matches D108's reason and O11's summary.

options.label: As is: never-retried list
options.description: The bound and the retried set are written in OP-01's spec now, before the landing flow places them. That goes against D108's own reason.
